ort: And then one day he said to her, "Sarah, I think I ort to go to the horspitral--I can't see--my eyes is painin' me so bad.

The neighbors ain't so fren'ly ez it seems they 'd ort to be;
They seem to be a-lookin' kinder sideways like at me,
"Yo' ort to tek dis as a warnin'," she said, "an' steady yo'self.
Yo' heart ort to prick yo' till yo' las' dyin' day fuh all yo' do to me an' my po' chirrun--"
Dey ort tuh lock he up, dey ort tuh get he 'n roast he behind fuh he--"
Wuh, Bright, yo' ort to be shame o' yo'self, man, fightin' ovah a chigga-foot gal."
orter:
An' I 'd lak to tell you 'bout it--what we had--but I ain't able,
Mention jes' a few things, dough I know I had n't orter,
Fu' I know 't will staht a hank'rin' an' yo' mouf 'll 'mence to worter.

But when they handed her the book I vow I was n't jealous.
We sung a hymn, an' Parson Brown dismissed us like he orter,
Fur, la! he 'd learned a thing er two an' made his blessin' shorter.

An' when I git a notion fixed, I 'm great on stickin' to it.
So when they giv' the next word out--I had n't orter tell it,
But then 't was all fur Nettie's sake--I missed so's she could spell it.
orthography:
Strangers strolled and spelled
At the lone orthography
Of the elder dead.

ortherings: “If there’s to be fresh ortherings—just when I getten used to two maisters, if I mun hev’ a mistress set o’er my heead, it’s like time to be flitting.
orthoptera: We are singularly rich in orthoptera: I don’t know whether—Ah! you have got hold of that glass jar—you are looking into that instead of my drawers.
orthodoxy: To us, what is termed orthodoxy is merely a facile unintelligent acquiescence; but to them, and in their hands, it was a terrible and paralysing tyranny.
